caption: The drawing depicts a weather vane mounted on a vertical rod with ornamental features. The main component is an arrow, colored gold, pointing to the right, with the year "1879" inscribed in black on the left-facing blade. The arrow is attached to a black vertical rod, which is topped with a gold sphere near its upper end. Just below the arrow, there are four gold letters—N, E, S, and W—denoting the cardinal directions, each facing outward from the center and arranged in a cross formation. Ornamental scrollwork, colored in black, extends outward and downward from the central rod, curving and interlacing below the direction letters. A larger gold sphere is mounted near the lower end of the rod, above a lightly sketched cloud-like base in gray. In the bottom left corner, there is a smaller, sketched inset showing a simplified version of the weather vane with notations for its height (10’-0”) and width (4’-0”). The entire drawing is enclosed within a rectangular border outlined in pale red. The artist's name and a number are inscribed in the lower right corner in red ink. The background of the drawing is off-white.
title: Weather Vane
